title: Western Toilet vs. Indian Toilet: Which is Better?
metaTitle: Western Toilet vs Indian Toilet: Which is Better?
description: Western toilet vs Indian toilet explained! Learn key differences, advantages, and drawbacks to decide which toilet is best for your home and family.
bodyHtml:
Bathrooms are no longer just functional spaces; they are now an important part of modern lifestyle and home aesthetics. One of the most debated choices when building or renovating a bathroom in India is: Should you go for a Western toilet or an Indian toilet?

Both have unique benefits, cultural relevance, and practical considerations. In this blog, we’ll give you a complete comparison of Western vs. Indian toilets, including design, comfort, health impact, cost, and maintenance. By the end, you’ll know which option is right for your needs — and why Prayag is the best sanitaryware brand in India to choose from.

What is a Western Toilet?

A Western toilet (also known as a commode) allows the user to sit, much like sitting on a chair. It is paired with a flush tank and sometimes comes with additional features such as soft-close seats, wall-hung designs, or bidet attachments.

Popular Types of Western Toilets:

  1. Floor-mounted commodes – Common in Indian homes.

  2. Wall-hung toilets – Give a floating look, easier to clean underneath.

  3. One-piece toilets – Sleek, modern, and compact design.

  4. Smart toilets – Sensor-based flushing, heated seats, bidet functions.

What is an Indian Toilet?

An Indian toilet is designed for squatting. The toilet pan is installed at floor level, and users squat to use it. Traditionally, water is stored in a bucket with a mug, though many modern Indian toilets are connected to flush tanks.

Popular Types of Indian Toilets:

  1. Orissa Pan (Ceramic) – The most widely used in India.

  2. Stainless Steel Pan – Durable and hygienic, often seen in public spaces.

  3. Anglo-Indian Toilets – A hybrid that allows both sitting and squatting.

Western Toilets: Advantages & Disadvantages

✅ Advantages

  • Convenience for All Ages: Ideal for kids, elderly, and people with mobility issues.

  • Hygienic Enhancements: Compatible with jet sprays, health faucets, and smart features.

  • Modern Look: Fits perfectly with luxury bathroom aesthetics.

  • Time-Saving: Quicker to use, especially in busy lifestyles.

❌ Disadvantages

  • Water Consumption: Uses 6–10 liters per flush on average.

  • Higher Cost: Both the unit and maintenance are expensive compared to Indian toilets.

  • Clogging Issues: Can get blocked if not maintained properly.

  • Space Requirement: Needs more space than Indian toilets.

Indian Toilets: Advantages & Disadvantages

✅ Advantages

  • Health Benefits: Squatting posture is scientifically proven to aid digestion and prevent constipation.

  • Water-Efficient: Requires only 2–3 liters per flush.

  • Durability: Fewer mechanical parts, making it long-lasting.

  • Lower Cost: Affordable to install and maintain.

  • Cultural Familiarity: Many Indians find squatting natural and comfortable.

❌ Disadvantages

  • Accessibility Issues: Difficult for elderly, pregnant women, or people with knee/joint pain.

  • Less Stylish: Doesn’t align with luxury bathroom aesthetics.

  • Learning Curve: Not convenient for international guests or urban populations used to Western toilets.

Health Aspects: Squatting vs. Sitting

  • Squatting (Indian toilets): Encourages a natural 35° angle between thighs and torso, which straightens the rectum for easier bowel movement. Helps reduce constipation, hemorrhoids, and colon issues.

  • Sitting (Western toilets): More comfortable but can sometimes cause incomplete evacuation if posture isn’t correct. Using footstools (like the “squatty potty”) with Western toilets can mimic squatting benefits.

Cost & Maintenance Comparison

Which Toilet is Better?

  • Choose a Western toilet if:
    ✅ You want comfort, modern aesthetics, and accessibility.
    ✅ Your household has elderly members or children.
    ✅ You live in an urban area with good water supply.

  • Choose an Indian toilet if:
    ✅ You want better digestion and natural squatting health benefits.
    ✅ You prefer low-cost, durable, water-saving solutions.
    ✅ You live in rural/semi-urban areas where maintenance is minimal.

👉 Many Indian families today are opting for a hybrid approach — having at least one Western toilet and one Indian toilet for maximum convenience.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

1. Which toilet is more hygienic – Western or Indian?

Both can be hygienic if maintained properly. Western toilets are easier to clean daily, while Indian toilets reduce direct skin contact.

2. Which toilet saves more water?

Indian toilets use less water (2–3 liters per flush) compared to Western toilets (6–10 liters per flush).

3. Can elderly people use Indian toilets?

It can be difficult for elderly people with knee or back pain. Western toilets or Anglo-Indian hybrid models are more suitable.

4. What is an Anglo-Indian toilet?

It is a hybrid toilet that can be used in both sitting and squatting positions — combining the best of both worlds.

5. Which is better for health – squatting or sitting?

Squatting (Indian toilets) has proven digestive benefits, but Western toilets offer comfort. Using a footrest with Western toilets can mimic squatting benefits.

Conclusion

The choice between a Western toilet vs. an Indian toilet depends on lifestyle, comfort, and budget. Indian toilets are healthier and water-efficient, while Western toilets are modern, convenient, and accessible.
